Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (security lead) and Jonas (infrastructure) so we can put together a short evidence packet. Quick answers up front and we will follow with attachments and a control mapping CSV: 

1) BYO-KMS: Yes. We support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault. We support HSM-backed CMKs (AWS CloudHSM, Cloud KMS HSM tiers) and envelope encryption patterns where the customer root key is used to encrypt service-level data keys. For our Dedicated/Private deployments we also provide an option to integrate with on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11 gateway.

2) Rotation: Data keys are rotated automatically every 90 days by default; CMKs are typically on a 1–2 year rotation cadence unless customer policy dictates otherwise. Root key rotation for BYO-KMS is customer-controlled. We will include rotation logs and our policy excerpt.

3) Separation of duties: KMS access follows least-privilege IAM roles. We maintain immutable audit logs for KMS operations (Create/Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) stored for 2 years in a write-once bucket with restricted access. For HSM-backed keys we log HSM administrative sessions and have multi-admin approval for key import.

4) Key escrow: Redwood does not retain plaintext customer root keys for BYO-KMS. For hosted-managed keys, we store wrapped keys; plaintext ever-present keys are never stored. Recovery flows are documented — will attach the recovery playbook.

5) Artifacts: we will provide the following: control_mapping_kms.csv (mapping of RFP sections to our controls), kms_arch_diagram.png (logical diagram showing envelope encryption), and soc2_snapshot_2027Q4.pdf (excerpted report showing control audit traces).

Action: Karthik / Jonas — can you assemble the CSV, the rotation log excerpt (redacted), and the HSM import approval screenshots? I will draft an email back to Alex with attachments and a short narrative for the procurement team.

Thanks,
Irene
